Defines canonical priority constants for deterministic execution ordering within the S.O.S event bus API Pipeline Execution Order Event handlers are dispatched in ascending order of their numerical priority weight Priority Tier Weight Recommended Purpose System — Low-level lifecycle orchestration window closing and profile tearing down State — Data store synchronization and model mutations before views react Default 0.0 — Standard domain logic and general third-party mod event listeners UI 1.0 — Primary GUI reconstruction widget refreshes and layout reflows PostUI 2.0 — Post-render effects animation sequence triggers telemetry and diagnostics Fractional In-Between Prioritization Because priorities are represented as normalized double-precision floating-point numbers rounded to 4 decimal places developers can insert handlers between standard tiers e.g EventPriority.State 0.5 for history navigation stacks or EventPriority.UI 0.1 for pre-render setup without risking key collisions or precision drift in the underlying Red-Black tree API On Prefab CommKeys SelectTarget prefab UpdateDataModel prefab EventPriority State API On Prefab CommKeys SelectTarget prefab RefreshCustomPanel prefab EventPriority UI

State priority tier Dispatched to synchronize configurations caches and data stores before visual components react Handlers at this level update data models selected targets and active configs Guaranteed to execute before Default domain listeners and UI layout renderers

System priority tier Dispatched first to handle critical infrastructure lifecycle termination and profile switching Handlers registered at this tier run before any data state mutations occur Reserved primarily for internal controller cleanup and low-level system coordination

Default priority tier 0.0 The neutral baseline tier for standard domain logic and general mod event handlers Used when no explicit priority order is specified in API.On(string, Action, double) or API.On<T>(string, Action<T>, double) Suitable for standard game logic that does not require specialized pre- or post-processing guarantees

Post-UI priority tier 2.0 Dispatched after primary visual components have completed their layout and drawing passes Ideal for initiating visual transitions triggering GUI.GUIAnimSequence animations executing diagnostics or logging telemetry where visual elements must already be present in the active hierarchy

UI priority tier 1.0 Dispatched to update construct or re-render graphical user interface components Handlers at this level are guaranteed to run after System and State handlers have fully committed their changes Visual controls reading from the state store such as API.GetState<T>(string) will always receive freshly updated data

Every method needs to receive as first parameter string key bridge key or identifier as first parameter The common keys are defined and documented in the static class SOS.CommKeys 1 Shared data Registration After creating and defining your class you will have to register it to the SOS API so that it is recognized and validated For that there are two main ways to register a new module to SOS 1 Automatic Registration Using the SOS.AutoRegisterAttribute attribute over an SOS module class that implements some ISOS* interface for automatic registration the first time the SOS window is opened never before passing the optional registration properties string id The unique identifier for your type if another object of the same type tries to register later with the same identifier it will be overwritten Default type.FullName type.Name If you register an SOS module with the same name as a previous one it will be overwritten keep it in mind if you wish to overwrite SOS modules from other mods for custom logic double order Order of execution or call Ascending order they are called from lowest to highest if it is equal it is treated alphabetically by the Id allowing them to be ordered in the calls in a predictable way Default 0 bool active Indicates if by default this SOS module will be executed or not It allows adding activation/deactivation logic of SOS modules for conditional logic or allowing the player to consciously deactivate SOS modules so as not to overload their interface with information that they do not need Default True Using this method the class is discovered automatically It is the idiomatic way to register classes that implement our interfaces Since this method does not require executing manual code to register the classes the Plugin class can be completely obviated if your mod s objective is only to add content to SOS 2 Manual registration Using any API.Register method e.g SOS.API.RegisterStatInfo and passing an object that represents the instantiation method and the same optional properties previously described after the object obj id order active You can register generic objects and Lua tables that implement directly or indirectly the contract s methods There are several ways to register an SOS module class T Direct instance of an object that implements the contract This is the simplest way to pass a single global instance and avoid instantiating Func T Pass a function that returns the instance that is wanted useful to pass a single instance with a custom method for instantiation for example compatibility with the singleton pattern or a custom factory object Generic objects that do not implement the contract directly or Lua tables(Lua compatibility) In these cases reflection is used to try to link the methods of the received instance with the methods that the contract requires using a custom proxy object.Cast T allowing to register indirectly classes without the need of making a hard reference to the S.O.S SDK simply obtaining by reflection the manual registration method API.Register and passing an object that fulfills the contract indirectly by method name Every unknown pattern falls in this branch and therefore it will try to be cast using the property and the method names over this object(or its target if it is a DuckProxy) Do not try to register arbitrary types that clearly do not fulfill the contract nor register in an indefinite loop because it could penalize the performance Make sure that they are valid Func object Delegate to register an instance builder using a generic object that implements the interface indirectly or a Lua table Type T Pass a class type that implements the instance s contract It is the default method used by the automatic registration Type object Pass a SOS Modules This section will teach you the different types of interfaces or contracts that any SOS Module needs or admits An SOS module is any class that implements some ISOS* interface SOS.ISOSTab SOS.ISOSStatInfo SOS.ISOSPrefab SOS.ISOSConfig SOS.ISOSWindowProfile For Lua the contract is practically the same as in C except the registration It does not admit the SOS.AutoRegisterAttribute attribute so it is mandatory to pass a Lua table that implements the contract s methods using any API.Register method e.g the HelloTab example from Getting Started That is why the later examples are written only in C but they apply in the same way to Lua To create your own SOS modules you need to create a public class that implements the corresponding contract either directly or indirectly generic by name/parameters of methods and afterwards register it via SOS.AutoRegisterAttribute or API.Register See Registration 1 Stat Info ISOSStatInfo Section of the inspector wiki that draws rows of information about the selected prefab If the rectT has no children it is cleaned Usage example And its localization in your mod s Localization/English.xml We recommend returning early with return when the prefab does not contain relevant data so the section is not drawn with nothing relevant 2 Central Tabs ISOSTab Central inspection tab for an entity type It appears in the tab bar only when SOS.ISOSTab.CanHandle returns true for the current target Usage example And its localization in the Localization/English.xml GUITab ensures that Update is never called before Init but it is always good practice to check for nulls 3 Prefab Providers ISOSPrefab Data provider that feeds the side browser with a new type of entity e.g JobPrefab EventPrefab TalentPrefab CharacterPrefab etc The browser groups its prefabs by runtime type and resolves each header from localization Type header you only need to serve them with SOS.ISOSPrefab.GetPrefabs Usage example The header of your section is resolved by itself from localization sos.prefab Type header e.g sos.prefab.jobprefab.header → If the key is missing the humanized type name is used Use the filter tokens filter.General filter.Mod filter.Category etc so that your provider responds to the browser s advanced search 4 Configs ISOSConfig Extensible configuration unit with persistence and declarative rendering in the settings window Inherit from SOS.Configs.ConfigDirtySaver for automated management and saving of changes Usage example Each setting must be declared in your mod s configuration XML And its localization in your mod s Localization/English.xml We recommend that you convert your SOS.ISOSConfig into a Singleton manual registration so that the initialization only happens a single time besides allowing direct accesses like most of our base configuration Modules do SOS.ISettingBaseExt.SetIfNotEqual is a helper that saves the property only if there was no real change allowing SOS.Configs.ConfigDirtySaver to do its work SOS.Configs.ConfigDirtySaver will be discussed in depth in the future SOS.ISOSConfig.Reset and SOS.ISOSConfig.Draw bring a default implementation you can obviate them if your SOS module does not need visible settings 5 Window Profiles ISOSWindowProfile Interchangeable visual layout of the SOS window You can create any visual style for example a single-column view a compact inspector or a floating tool with only the essentials It inherits from SOS.GUI.GUIWindow and can be changed via SOS.API.Emit SOS.CommKeys.ChangeProfile id It is completely free to modify the appearance of the window completely Usage example The name and the description of the dropdown are resolved from localization id name id desc in your mod s Localization/English.xml You can read the current code in the repository for more detail Optionally you can define SOS.ISOSWindowProfile.ProfileConfig a specific configuration for this Module where it will be called after the SOS.ISOSConfig WindowProfileConfig module is saved and it will draw its SOS.ISOSConfig.Draw() inside this configuration in the specific area given by it Definition example Reset is affected by WindowProfileConfig and the general reset Recommendations and good practices We do NOT recommend implementing several types of SOS modules in the same class we consider this an anti-pattern and currently it will lead to creating 2 instances of the same class for each type of contract(Unless you manually register the same instance or delegate for both, but we do not recommend it either) Each SOS module works as a single-instance builder by default which means that the same instance is used until the SOS window is closed/reopened Keep it in mind if you consider saving information in the class that it does not interfere when being
